chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak from Abdullah ibn Jabalah from Sama'ah from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I said to him, 'For a man who has children, is it permissible for him to leave his wealth to his relatives?' He said, 'It is his wealth; he does with it what he wishes until death comes to him.'

key_terms.يَصْنَعُ بِهِ مَا شَاءَ: he does with it what he wishes

ai.seo_question: Can a man with children leave his entire wealth to relatives in his will?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of testamentary freedom (al-wasiyya) is affirmed, distinguishing it from the fixed shares of inheritance (al-faraid) by granting the testator full discretion over his wealth until death. This hadith is central to the Shia legal discussion on whether a bequest to heirs requires the consent of other heirs, with this text supporting the view that the owner's will prevails in the discretionary portion. It highlights the flexibility in estate planning within the framework of Islamic law, allowing for charitable or specific familial distributions beyond the obligatory shares.
